purpose: Bounded common-career coverage audit against primary occupational and Texas licensing sources; candidates are not yet implementation-ready financial profiles.
method: Compared named profile titles and SOC mappings in current finance-data plus existing custom profiles against familiar student-facing careers across health, learning, computing, public service, trades, business, design, engineering and performing arts. This is an editorial coverage screen, not an exhaustive list of all BLS occupations.

candidates.title: Nurse practitioner
candidates.typicalPreparation: RN preparation followed by graduate NP education, commonly MSN or DNP.
candidates.texasMinimumOrProtectedCredential: Texas RN license/compact privilege, approved advanced-practice education, congruent national certification, APRN license, and application eligibility. Prescriptive authority has additional requirements.
candidates.training: Clinical preparation in a defined patient population and specialty.
candidates.earningsCaveat: Keep NP wages separate from RN, PA and nurse-anesthetist wages. Entry means entry to qualified NP work, not entry to nursing.

candidates.title: Elementary school teacher
candidates.typicalPreparation: Bachelor’s degree plus approved teacher preparation.
candidates.texasMinimumOrProtectedCredential: Standard Texas classroom certificate route: bachelor’s, approved preparation, assignment-specific exams, state application and fingerprinting. Statutory employment exceptions are not the standard preparation target.
candidates.training: Elementary curriculum and child development with supervised classroom practice.
candidates.earningsCaveat: District salary schedules often apply across grade bands; show the district contract/year and do not add an assumed grade-level premium.

candidates.title: High school teacher
candidates.typicalPreparation: Bachelor’s degree plus approved teacher preparation.
candidates.texasMinimumOrProtectedCredential: Standard Texas classroom certificate route: bachelor’s, approved preparation, assignment-specific exams, state application and fingerprinting. Statutory employment exceptions are not the standard preparation target.
candidates.training: A teaching subject and adolescent learning with supervised classroom practice.
candidates.earningsCaveat: District salary schedules often apply across grade bands; show the district contract/year and do not add an assumed grade-level premium.

candidates.title: Computer user support specialist
candidates.typicalPreparation: Some college courses, IT certificate, associate’s or bachelor’s depending on technical depth; some enter with high school plus relevant certifications.
candidates.texasMinimumOrProtectedCredential: No universal degree or Texas professional license minimum is established by the reviewed occupational source; employers set technical requirements.
candidates.training: Troubleshooting, customer communication, operating systems and vendor tools.
candidates.earningsCaveat: Do not use network support or software-developer wages for user support.

candidates.title: Police patrol officer
candidates.typicalPreparation: High school/GED plus approved peace-officer academy and field training; college can add preparation and advancement options.
candidates.texasMinimumOrProtectedCredential: TCOLE academy/eligibility, licensing exam and appointment requirements. Standard minimum age is 21, with qualifying college/military exceptions at 18; medical, psychological and background standards apply.
candidates.training: Approved basic peace-officer course and employing-agency field training.
candidates.earningsCaveat: Austin agency pay, overtime and specialty stipends differ from metro employee wages. Do not treat overtime as assured base salary.

candidates.title: Firefighter
candidates.typicalPreparation: Fire academy plus emergency medical preparation; community-college fire science can complement training.
candidates.texasMinimumOrProtectedCredential: TCFP basic structure certification route includes approved training, qualifying exam results, medical-response training, fingerprints and application. Hiring departments may set higher standards.
candidates.training: Firefighter and hazardous-material skills; medical preparation at accepted EMR/ECA/EMT/paramedic level.
candidates.earningsCaveat: Base municipal pay differs from overtime, shift hours and paramedic stipends; volunteer roles do not imply an employed annual wage.

candidates.title: Welder
candidates.typicalPreparation: High school/GED plus technical and supervised on-the-job training; certificate/associate routes available.
candidates.texasMinimumOrProtectedCredential: The reviewed source does not establish a universal Texas occupational license. Employers and project codes can require process/material-specific qualification.
candidates.training: Safe welding techniques, blueprint reading, measurement and supervised practice.
candidates.earningsCaveat: Specialty pipeline/travel/overtime pay is not the typical entry baseline. Separate employees from independent contracting.

candidates.title: Heavy and tractor-trailer truck driver
candidates.typicalPreparation: Truck-driving school or an employer training route leading to the appropriate CDL.
candidates.texasMinimumOrProtectedCredential: Texas CLP/CDL, required knowledge/skills tests and applicable medical qualification. First-time Class A/B applicants ordinarily need ELDT through a registered provider; CLP minimum holding period 14 days.
candidates.training: Vehicle inspection, control and road driving; endorsements depend on vehicle/cargo.
candidates.earningsCaveat: Employee driver wages are not owner-operator revenue. Fuel, truck financing, maintenance and unpaid time must be deducted from business receipts.

candidates.title: Real estate sales agent
candidates.typicalPreparation: Qualifying real-estate courses and practical sales/business preparation; college is optional.
candidates.texasMinimumOrProtectedCredential: TREC age18+, eligibility/fitness, 180 classroom hours, application/fingerprints, licensing examination, and licensed broker sponsorship before active sales work.
candidates.training: Contracts, agency, finance and supervised brokerage work.
candidates.earningsCaveat: Commission income is variable; employee wage surveys exclude many self-employed agents. Gross commissions are not take-home income.

candidates.title: Interior designer
candidates.typicalPreparation: Bachelor’s in interior design or related training is typical.
candidates.texasMinimumOrProtectedCredential: Texas protects the Registered Interior Designer credential. Registration requires qualifying education/experience, all NCIDQ sections and Board application/background requirements. Do not describe every unregistered decorator as illegally practicing.
candidates.training: Space planning, codes, accessibility, CAD/BIM and portfolio work.
candidates.earningsCaveat: Employee design wages exclude self-employed business income; furniture sales commissions may use another occupation.

candidates.title: Web and digital interface designer
candidates.typicalPreparation: Education ranges from high school to bachelor’s; portfolio and demonstrated design skill matter.
candidates.texasMinimumOrProtectedCredential: No universal degree or Texas professional license minimum is established by the occupational source. Employer and project requirements vary.
candidates.training: User interfaces, accessibility, prototypes and usability testing.
candidates.earningsCaveat: Use this specific occupation; graphic-design and software-development wages do not establish UI-designer pay.

candidates.title: Chemical engineer
candidates.typicalPreparation: Bachelor’s in chemical engineering or a related engineering field; internships/co-op help.
candidates.texasMinimumOrProtectedCredential: PE is required for regulated engineering practice subject to Texas statutory exemptions; not every entry-level industrial engineering job requires PE.
candidates.training: Chemistry, physics, mathematics, process design and laboratory/project work.
candidates.earningsCaveat: Austin occupational wages may be sparse; Houston/Dallas fallback must be labeled geography and not blended into an Austin observation.

candidates.title: Aerospace engineer
candidates.typicalPreparation: Bachelor’s in aerospace engineering or a related engineering field.
candidates.texasMinimumOrProtectedCredential: No universal entry-level PE requirement; regulated engineering scope follows Texas licensing law/exemptions. Defense roles may require security clearance and some clearances require U.S. citizenship.
candidates.training: Flight/space systems, mechanics, controls, mathematics and engineering projects.
candidates.earningsCaveat: Do not imply a security clearance is required for every aerospace job. Metro wages do not guarantee local openings.

candidates.title: Photographer
candidates.typicalPreparation: High school is typical entry education; classes, certificates or degrees can develop technical/artistic skill.
candidates.texasMinimumOrProtectedCredential: No universal degree or Texas professional license minimum is established by the reviewed occupational source. Business and activity-specific permissions are separate.
candidates.training: Camera/lighting, editing, portfolio, client work and business practice.
candidates.earningsCaveat: Part-time/self-employment is common. Employee hourly wages exclude self-employment and do not guarantee 2,080 paid hours.

candidates.title: Musician or singer
candidates.typicalPreparation: Extensive training and practice; no universal formal credential. Classical/opera routes may include bachelor’s or graduate study.
candidates.texasMinimumOrProtectedCredential: No universal degree or Texas professional license minimum is established by the occupational source.
candidates.training: Instrument/voice instruction, rehearsal, auditions and live/recording experience.
candidates.earningsCaveat: Hourly performance wage is not full-time annual earnings. Paid gigs can be irregular and preparation time unpaid; self-employed income is excluded from employee wage data.

candidates.title: Actor
candidates.typicalPreparation: Acting classes, sustained practice and auditions; formal degree is not universal.
candidates.texasMinimumOrProtectedCredential: No universal degree or Texas professional license minimum is established by the occupational source.
candidates.training: Performance technique, productions, audition preparation and portfolio/reel.
candidates.earningsCaveat: Short engagements and periods without paid work are common. Do not annualize hourly employee wages at 2,080 hours or imply celebrity income.

candidates.title: Veterinary technician
candidates.typicalPreparation: Technician usually associate degree in veterinary technology; technologist commonly bachelor’s.
candidates.texasMinimumOrProtectedCredential: Texas LVT is a protected credential, not a blanket requirement for every animal-care assistant. LVT route: AVMA-accredited program, VTNE, state board exam, fingerprinting and application.
candidates.training: Supervised animal nursing, laboratory tests and clinical practice under a veterinarian.
candidates.earningsCaveat: Use technician wages rather than veterinarian pay; the occupation also includes technologists.

candidates.title: Radiologic technologist
candidates.typicalPreparation: Associate’s degree in radiography with clinical preparation is typical.
candidates.texasMinimumOrProtectedCredential: Texas general medical radiologic technologist certificate and qualifying education/exam/application requirements for regulated radiologic procedures. MRI-only practice has a distinct licensing scope.
candidates.training: Patient positioning, radiation safety and supervised imaging practice.
candidates.earningsCaveat: Radiologic technologist, MRI technologist and sonographer are distinct occupations and salary categories.

implementationGate: Verify current Austin wage series or labeled Dallas/Houston fallback before salary cards.
Acquire credential-specific education cost example and training duration.
Separate legal/protected-title requirements from typical hiring preferences.
Performing-arts hourly earnings require irregular-work scenarios, not 2,080-hour annualization.
Do not reuse a generic interest match as proof of aptitude or future career success.

verifiedTeacherTaxonomy.note: Existing middle-school SOC mapping is correct; elementary/high-school are separate profiles, not aliases.
